data.claim: After the splits, the five hot paths (each old file plus every module that replaced it) block fewer ready items per day, and take a smaller share of all glob blocking, than before; lease minutes per day on the old file names fall.
data.falsifier: Blocked item-hours per day on the five paths (old file + all successors) after the split at or above the before figure, or their share of all blocking not falling. Retrospective note: this falsifier was written after the first probe pass had been read, not before, and there is no control group: load and the backlog changed in the same period, and a second split wave (r-small-files, 2026-10-31..11-01) turned config.py, surfaces/mcp.py and core/records.py into packages too.
data.mechanism: Claims edit one module of a package rather than one shared file, so two tasks in the same domain stop overlapping; a lease is exclusive per glob, so fewer leases naming one path means fewer refusals.
data.probe: Two scripts over all of .ddflow/events/*.jsonl on 2026-11-04, main e234caf3c (log 2026-09-28..11-04; before = up to 2026-10-06T05:00Z, 7.9 days; after = 29.7 days; last14d = subset of after). (1) lease minutes: per lease.acquired, intervals to lease.released/expired or item.completed/abandoned, capped at last renew + ttl_s, per glob from when it joined the lease, matched by fnmatch. (2) replay: every 2 h rebuild items (task.added/updated, needs, parent phase needs, done/abandoned/blocked) and live leases (renew+ttl), ready = needs done and not leased, blocked = any glob overlapping a live lease by ddflow.core.globs.overlap, attributed to the path. Sizes: git show <ref>:<path> | wc -l. lease.waiting exists only from 2026-10-16, so it cannot give a before/after figure and is not used for one.
